text:
carmen (partnerops): Heads-up: EdgeScale reported messed-up entitlements in today's preview. They send per-region customer_id (cus-us-west-1 vs cus-us-east-1) but our partner mapping collapsed them to a single marketplace customer_id, so some usage double-counted across regions.

lee (eng): do we have sample events?

carmen (partnerops): redacted snippet:
```json
{"partner_customer_id":"cus-us-west-1","usage":300,"utc_reported_at":"2026-05-02T02:10:00Z","event_id":"e-9001"}
{"partner_customer_id":"cus-us-east-1","usage":300,"utc_reported_at":"2026-05-02T02:10:05Z","event_id":"e-9001"}
```
(note same event_id, different partner_customer_id namespace).

ivan (billing): that caused invoice_preview to show two separate accounts billed and also combined under one marketplace account later, leading to +$120 unexpected. not good for go-live customers.

maya (marketplace): partner contract says partner_customer_id should be canonical per customer; EdgeScale says they historically sharded IDs per region and relied on us to map them. ambiguity now surfaced when their edge retry dedup didn't include region.

lee (eng): short-term mitigation: pause EdgeScale hourly feed and request resend that includes partner_customer_global_id in payload. also ask them to include region in event_id (e.g., e-9001:us-west).

carmen (partnerops): i've asked for resend; ETA 1.5h.

lee (eng): medium-term changes on our side: 1) partner_profiles table accepts customer_id_aliases (list) and partner_customer_namespace flag; 2) ingest canonicalizer expands event namespace to "{partner_id}:{region}:{event_id}" when partner indicates region-scoped event_ids; 3) dedupe by canonical_event_key = hash(partner_id + canonical_event_id + utc_ts).

ivan (billing): backfill plan? we need to avoid double-crediting.

lee (eng): backfill plan (staging -> prod): run detection query to find event_id collisions across partner_customer_id aliases, mark suspected duplicates, then run idempotent adjustment that creates partner_ledger_corrections rather than deleting rows. sample detection SQL:
```sql
select event_id, array_agg(distinct partner_customer_id) as seen_ids, sum(usage) as total_usage
from partner_ledger
where partner_id='edgescale' and ingested_at >= '2026-05-02T00:00:00Z' and ingested_at < '2026-05-03T00:00:00Z'
group by event_id
having count(distinct partner_customer_id) > 1;
```
Then for each event_id flagged, create a correction row with negative usage for duplicates and a single canonical positive row, and then run invoice_preview_recompute for affected marketplace_customer_ids.

maya (marketplace): prefer corrections over deletions so audit trail remains. we should also publish a short partner-facing KB about canonical partner_customer_id and event_id namespacing.

sync-bot: action scheduled: pause-ingest edgescale at 2026-05-02T04:30:00Z by carmen.

lee (eng): I'll open an RFC for the canonical_event_key change and quick migration script. Low-risk: will gate on partner_profile flag so we don't change behavior for others.

carmen (partnerops): owners: lee (ingest + RFC + backfill), ivan (billing verification + corrections playbook), maya (catalog policy + partner KB), carmen (partner comms).

ivan (billing): once backfill runs, I will review invoice previews and if any customer preview delta > $25 we'll queue manual review.

carmen (partnerops): thanks, team — ping if you need access to EdgeScale dumps. :thumbsup:
